research_concepts: teammate DRIVE preceding PNR as a play-type sequence
derived play-type possession records in the graph database
methodological_questions: Do the inferred DRIVE and PNR labels identify real play types well enough to define a DRIVE-to-PNR sequence?
Is PNR PPP conditioned on a prior teammate DRIVE distinct from PNR PPP in general, after adjusting for player, shot quality, and context?
Do PNR labels depend on outcome data, so that conditioning on outcomes produces circularity?
Is the sample large enough for DRIVE-to-PNR sequences within the stated data versions, after accounting for playoff vs regular-season differences?

historical_evidence.finding: Sequence-level PPP by inferred play type produced an artifact: an assisted flag present only on makes gave SPOT_UP 2.83 PPP and TRANSITION 0.62 PPP. After the rewrite, SPOT_UP was about 1.16 and TRANSITION about 1.20. The record notes possible overlap with APP slices.

Foul-ending possessions inflated OTHER PPP (36% of OTHER ends in fouls). DRIVE was 12pp below the foul benchmark. PNR showed a 22% foul rate. Only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) mapped to a real play type via initiation_type.

Label accuracy and distribution audit gave overall verdict tool_eval_fail: OTHER was 20.2% against a target under 10%, 40.8% of labels were low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw was 1.7% against a 14-22% benchmark, most play types had PPP above the benchmark band, and MIA identity checks failed. Tagged LABEL_ERROR and LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD.

Backfilled label verification gave a final FAIL. PNR was 28.7% against a 20-28% band, PULL_UP was 7.9%, 3,100 games had team PNR above 33%, team identity failed, and 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated. PNR PPP of 0.948 passed, as did the temporal check, over 921,514 possessions.

Play-type PPP across playoff series game buckets was observational with selection caveats, over 1,197 records without CIs. PNR changed +0.087 and DRIVE +0.060 from early to late series. The record states NO CLEAR SIGNAL.
Regular-season DRIVE PPP (1.198) exceeded playoff DRIVE PPP (0.912), a -0.286 difference across 25 teams. PNR changed -0.173. This concerns regular season vs playoffs, not DRIVE-to-PNR sequencing.
2024-25 shot-level PNR shares of half-court shots ranged from about 7.6% to 13.8% across teams. The rates are a calibration input for PBPProxyPNR, and the output had no pass/fail gate.
Playoff defenses lowered DRIVE allowed PPP (-0.268) and share, while PNR share rose +12.1pp. The record says the PNR share jump may reflect tagging differences. No inferential test was run.
On-ball coverage labels were sparse: 14.9% confidently labeled for DET and 3.3% for ORL. The NBA matchups feed did not populate switches_on.
Routing comparison yielded 8 divergences with 0 scoreable, because the players were missing from Neo4j.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Sequence-level PPP by inferred play type computed before the labeler was fixed
failed_approaches.why: A construction flaw (assisted flag present only on makes) produced an apparent effect; recorded as C_artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type PPP comparison using initiation_type-derived labels
failed_approaches.why: Foul endings contaminated OTHER and DRIVE, and initiation_type mapped only 0.7% of possessions to a real play type; recorded as C_artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type label accuracy and distribution audit
failed_approaches.why: Systematic label error and leakage into OTHER; the record's verdict is tool_eval_fail, with LABEL_ERROR, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER risks noted.
Distributions failed their bands and team identity failed; most PNR labels were proxy-calibrated rather than observed.
Labels were too sparse to test and the switches_on field did not populate; recorded as untestable.

evidence_establishes: Play-type labels in this project have documented, recurring label and leakage problems: foul leakage into OTHER and DRIVE, outcome-dependent flags, low initiation_type coverage, and proxy-calibrated PNR labels.
No retrieved record tests whether a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR changes PNR PPP. The sequencing question has not been answered by any retrieved study.
Related retrieved work (SF-APPS-011, SF-APPS-010, SF-APPS-012) concerns contexts such as regular season vs playoffs and series progression, and does not establish a sequencing effect.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether DRIVE-to-PNR sequences can be reliably identified from the current labels, since no record reports the validated accuracy of sequence labels.
The size of any sequencing effect, its sign, or its confidence interval.
Whether PNR PPP after a DRIVE differs from PNR PPP in general once player and shot quality are controlled.
Whether the derived graph records carry the ordering and attribution needed for teammate-level sequences in every data version.
own_inferences: The question as posed is a sequence claim, and the labels that define both sides of it are the ones the retrieved records repeatedly flag as unreliable. A test would inherit that unreliability.
Conditioning on PNR possessions that already have a derived outcome, or on proxy-calibrated PNR labels, risks leakage and circular PPP comparisons.
Playoff vs regular-season and series-stage differences in DRIVE and PNR PPP could confound a pooled sequencing estimate unless modelled explicitly.
A DRIVE-then-PNR sequence is a sparse cell within a single team-game, so power is likely limited even with clean labels.
uncertainties: The retrieval returned no record that directly tests DRIVE-to-PNR sequencing, so the prior-work picture is incomplete.
I did not run data_catalog or read_family, so I do not know whether the per-game files carry the fields needed to order possessions and attribute the DRIVE to a teammate.
Sample counts for DRIVE-then-PNR sequences are unknown; no record reports them.
The reliability of the current PNR label after the recorded rewrites is not established by any retrieved record.

historical_effect.explanation: Before retrieval the question looked like a standard sequencing test on the derived play-type records. The retrieved records show that play-type labels here have repeated artifact and validation failures (SF-PAP-096, SF-CHT-025, SF-APPM-014, SF-APPA-030), and no record supports the sequencing effect. That moves the decision from proceed to do_not_proceed until labels are validated.

blocking_constraints.text: DRIVE and PNR labels have documented misclassification, OTHER inflation, and proxy calibration; no validated label accuracy exists for sequences.
Play-type labels are partly derived from outcomes (assisted flags, foul endings), so PPP conditioned on labels is circular.
Teammate DRIVE immediately followed by PNR within a possession sequence is likely a sparse cell; no record reports its count.
Player quality, shot quality, and playoff vs regular-season context can drive both the DRIVE and the PNR outcome.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved study tests whether a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP. Retrieved work covers label validity (SF-APPA-030, SF-APPM-014 tool_eval_fail, SF-CHT-025 artifact), playoff vs regular-season PPP (SF-APPS-011 supported), and series-stage PPP (SF-APPS-010 inconclusive). These bear on the inputs but do not answer the sequencing question.

risks.text: DRIVE and PNR labels have documented misclassification and proxy calibration (SF-APPM-014, SF-APPA-030).
Assisted flags and foul endings are derived from outcomes, so PNR PPP conditioned on labels can be circular (SF-PAP-096, SF-CHT-025).
Labels built from the full possession may use information from after the PNR begins (SF-APPM-014).
DRIVE-then-PNR sequences within a team-game may be too rare for stable PPP estimates.
Player quality, shot quality, and playoff vs regular-season context may drive both sides (SF-APPS-011, SF-APPS-012).
Players who take DRIVEs may differ systematically from those who set PNRs, and selection into play types may bias the estimate.
PNR share and PPP shift across tagging rewrites (SF-APPS-012, SF-APPM-058), so the measure is not stable across versions.
Sequence construction has produced artifacts before (SF-PAP-096, SF-APPS-009), so a new sequence builder needs verification.
The retrieved studies used small or unreported samples without CIs (SF-APPS-010, SF-APPS-011), so power is unknown.
Regular-season and playoff contexts differ (SF-APPS-011), and pooling across seasons may mix regimes.

design.estimand: Within-team, within-season difference in PNR PPP for possessions where a teammate DRIVE immediately precedes the PNR, relative to matched PNR possessions without a preceding DRIVE, adjusted for PNR-initiator, defender, shot-quality, and playoff status. Not to be run until the label gate is passed.
design.unit: Team-game PNR possession, with a binary indicator for an immediately preceding teammate DRIVE on the same possession chain.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 and the 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; playoffs kept as a separate stratum. Use only games where play-type labels pass a validation gate (label accuracy measured by hand-coded audit).
design.power: Not computable from the retrieved records. Pre-register a minimum detectable effect and the expected count of DRIVE-then-PNR sequences after the audit. Abort if the expected count is too small for the chosen MDE.
design.controls: Player and team fixed effects; shot distance and result excluded as outcome-adjacent covariates, or used only as pre-sequence context; defensive matchup context from the matchup fields; game context; and a placebo analysis on non-sequence pairs.
design.falsification: Placebo: same DRIVE-to-PNR test using a non-teammate or a time-shuffled DRIVE. Also run the test on labels from the pre-rewrite pipeline (SF-PAP-096 state) to confirm the effect disappears when the known artifact is present.
design.multiplicity: Single pre-registered primary contrast. Other play-type pairs and playoff splits are secondary and labelled exploratory, with a correction applied if reported.
design.decision_rule: Proceed only if (a) label accuracy passes a pre-registered audit on a hand-coded sample, (b) the expected sequence count meets the pre-registered MDE, and (c) the placebo shows no effect. Report the adjusted difference with a CI. Treat a positive result as supported only if it survives all three conditions. Otherwise report untestable or artifact.
design.data_version: Data as of 2026-06-14: 2022-23 to 2024-25 full seasons and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season, complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs, complete from 2026-06-21. Use only complete data versions and freeze label-pipeline version.

research_concepts: sequence effects of prior play type on subsequent play-type efficiency
methodological_questions: Does a teammate DRIVE immediately before a PNR raise PNR points per possession?
Are play-type labels derived from outcome data, creating label leakage or circularity?
Is the effect confounded by player quality, shot quality, possession context, or selection into play types?
Are the available per-game play-by-play fields sufficient to define DRIVE-to-PNR sequences reliably?
args.query: teammate drive preceding pick-and-roll points per possession play-type sequencing labeling data quality

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Field guidance:
- historical_evidence and failed_approaches: only records returned by a tool, with the status as recorded; empty lists
  if nothing relevant was returned.
- testability.p_testable: probability that the question can be answered with the stated data at useful statistical power.
- prior_work.already_answered: whether retrieved earlier work already answered substantially the same question.
  Use "unknown" if no earlier work was retrieved. List identifiers you relied on in prior_work.cited.
- predicted_outcome: probabilities (summing to 1) of what a competent test of the question as posed would conclude:
  supported, rejected (adequately powered null), untestable (cannot be tested with this data), artifact (apparent
  effect produced by a flaw), uncertain (inconclusive or inadequately tested).
- decision: proceed, proceed_with_changes (state the changes in design), or do_not_proceed.
- design: a pre-registration-quality plan even if the decision is do_not_proceed (then describe the minimum viable test).
